stem.text: The diagram shows part of a circuit that uses a potentiometer wire to measure a potential difference (p.d.) in an external circuit.

stem.alt: Circuit diagram of a potentiometer wire from X to Z, with a cell labelled E connected to the wire by a top wire carrying a current labelled I1. Point Y lies on the wire with a lead to Q, and point X has a lead to P carrying a current labelled I2. Printed labels: X, Y, Z, P, Q, E, I1, I2, L1, L2.

stem.text: The potentiometer wire XZ has length $L_1$. It is connected to a cell of known electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$ that has negligible internal resistance.
Terminals P and Q are connected to the external p.d. to be measured. The length of the potentiometer wire between points X and Y is $L_2$.
The ratio of the lengths $L_1$ and $L_2$ is used to determine the p.d. between P and Q in terms of $E$.
Which condition must be met in order to determine this p.d.?

C.text: The p.d. across YZ must be zero.

D.text: The resistance of the external circuit must be zero.
